title: Fail-closed production authority configuration

scope.authority_contract: Hosted environments require explicit authority declarations for identity, missions, policy, approvals, actions, outbox, receipts, usage and credentials.
scope.fail_closed: Staging and production reject absent authorities and memory, test or fixture backends; credentials require secret-manager and other authorities reject secret-manager.
scope.typed_failure: Hosted deployment planning raises UNSAFE_AUTHORITY_CONFIGURATION with exit code 10 for unsafe authority configuration; an actual hosted service bootstrap integration is not present in this local repository.
scope.local_compatibility: Sandbox/local configurations remain valid without hosted authority declarations, including custom sandbox slugs; malformed local authority maps remain ordinary validation failures rather than hosted startup errors.

acceptance_coverage: Hosted staging and production configuration validation cannot omit authority declarations, including custom slugs with declared hosted types.
Memory, test and fixture authorities are rejected for hosted environments.
Unknown authority keys are rejected rather than silently ignored.
Hosted credentials authority is constrained to secret-manager.
Unsafe hosted deployment fallback has a typed error and deterministic exit code; hosted process-bootstrap enforcement remains unproven.
A complete durable production declaration validates.
Local sandbox configuration remains valid without hosted authorities.
The existing Atlas package suite remains green.
remaining_gate_requirements: CI execution evidence required by the CI + disposable production-like stack gate
Authority census against deployed Atlas Cloud services and durable database, queue and secret-manager owners
Disposable production-like boot and negative fallback evidence, including hosted process-bootstrap enforcement
Hosted staging and production evidence required by later programme gates
Whole-product, capacity, provider, usage/cost, billing, commercial and certification evidence
absent_proof: Atlas Cloud authority census and one-writable-owner verification
verdict: ATLAS-BMR2-P4-001 is LOCAL_PROVEN but remains BLOCKED_EXTERNAL because CI, a disposable production-like stack and deployed authority ownership evidence are unavailable. No hosted or production readiness is claimed.
limitations: Absent proof remains: CI, disposable production-like stack, Atlas Cloud authority census and one-writable-owner verification, staging, production, provider sandbox, capacity, usage/cost ledger, billing settlement, commercial readiness, whole-product certification.
